summary: The ADV-D100-01 repair itself lands, and lands well: clause 3's role cell for the composite candidate is replaced by a special rule requiring each later owner-recording to name exactly one of DR-106, DR-109, or DR-113, with its own D-000 cycle and its own commit, and with recording or overturning one row expressly not reaching the other two. That is a verbatim match to the candidate artifact's own severability field, and it is reinforced in four independent places (clause 2's coverage test, clause 4's pin, clause 5's prohibition on bundling, and a new Alternatives rejection). Bundling is closed. But the repair was executed by rewriting 'candidate' to 'row' in the operative clauses, and one of the five eligible candidates has no row. deferral.windows-platform.preview.v2.json carries registerRow 'D-002 platform set - Windows'; D-096 clause 4 states outright that 'Windows is not a file-08 row and is not SATISFIED as one'; and file 08 contains no Windows row. I raised the loose turn-1 version of this as ADVISORY ADV-D100-C2-A1 and explicitly reasoned it could not open an authorization path. The turn-2 rewording defeats that reasoning. Clause 2's coverage test - the single precondition that gates whether a future D-096 (A) grant is applicable at all - is now keyed to 'every named role for the row being recorded'. For the Windows candidate there is no row, so the test admits a vacuous reading under which no role needs covering. That is not a blocked path, it is an open one, and it is new in turn 2. Clause 4 compounds it by making 'the single file-08 row being recorded' a mandatory pin with no referent, and clause 5 compounds it again by scoping the operative permission to 'the roles of the named row'. The subject's own Alternatives section still carries the turn-1 candidate-keyed wording, so the file now contradicts itself on the very test at issue. Every other attack line in the dispatch fails against the bytes, and all twelve cited digests plus three commits verify against live bytes.

findings.observation: Turn 1 keyed all three clauses to the candidate. Turn 2 keys all three to a file-08 row. Four of the five eligible candidates have a file-08 row (DR-108, DR-110, DR-116, and the three rows inside the composite draft). The fifth does not. deferral.windows-platform.preview.v2.json records registerRow as 'D-002 platform set - Windows' and whatThisDoesNotDo includes 'Does not edit file 08'; D-096 clause 4 reads 'The named rows stay OPEN. Windows is not a file-08 row and is not SATISFIED as one.'; and I grepped file 08 itself, whose only 'windows' occurrence is DR-111's unrelated 'compatibility windows'. Clause 3 nevertheless lists the Windows candidate as eligible and assigns it roles 'Product + release + platform', matching its ownerWhoMustRecord verbatim. So the file declares a candidate eligible and then states its preconditions, its pins, and its operative permission in terms of a referent that candidate does not have.
findings.whyBlocking: This is not the imprecision I passed at turn 1. Clause 2 is the applicability test for D-096 (A) - the one precondition standing between a future user grant and an owner-recording, and the mechanism by which D-096 clause 3 (A) is kept from being satisfied by an under-scoped grant. Keyed to the candidate, it demands the grant cover 'Product + release + platform' before Windows may be recorded. Keyed to the row, it demands the grant cover every named role 'for the row being recorded', and for Windows there is no row and therefore no roles named by a row. A drafter reading clause 2 literally can hold the coverage test vacuously satisfied for the Windows candidate by any adopted grant whatever. That is an authorization path, and it is exactly the path clause 2 exists to close. My turn-1 non-blocking rationale for the ancestor of this defect was that D-096 clause 4 and clause 5's no-edit-file-08 rule would refuse a drafter who reached for a row; that rationale answers the clause 4 and clause 5 legs, which merely block or misdirect, but it does not answer the clause 2 leg, which loosens rather than blocks. Independently, clauses 4 and 5 leave the mechanics unable to do their job for one of the five candidates they declare eligible: the mandatory row pin has no referent, and the operative permission in clause 5 reaches only 'the roles of the named row', so on its face it does not authorize the shape of recording the Windows candidate needs. A mechanics entry whose sole function is to state how later authorization-bearing entries must be written should not ship instructions that one fifth of its own eligible set cannot satisfy.
findings.corroboration: The subject contradicts itself on this exact point. The Alternatives section still carries the turn-1 wording: 'Expand eligible rows beyond the five D-096 candidates. Rejected: D-096 (A) must cover every named role **for the candidate being recorded**.' Operative clause 2 now says row; its own stated rationale says candidate. One of the two is wrong, and the rationale is the one that matches D-096 clause 3, which conditions owner-recording on a grant that 'expressly covers every named role for the candidate being recorded'.
findings.notTheFix: Deleting the Windows candidate from clause 3 would repair the contradiction but would narrow D-096's recorded set, which this entry states it does not overturn. The repair belongs in the wording, not the eligibility table.
findings.suggestedRepair: Restore candidate-keying as the base test and let the row rule be the composite candidate's special case. Clause 2: 'expressly covers every named role for the candidate being recorded, and where that candidate maps to a file-08 row, for the row being recorded (for the 106/109/113 candidate, the selected row's roles)'. Clause 4: 'the file-08 row being recorded, if the candidate has one (for 106/109/113, exactly one of those three; for the Windows platform set, none - it is not a file-08 row per D-096); the owner role(s) being recorded'. Clause 5: 'for the roles of the named row, or for the named platform set where the candidate is not a file-08 row'. This keeps the ADV-D100-01 landing fully intact - the composite candidate still yields exactly one row per entry, per cycle, per commit.

structuralObservation: The turn-2 delta is a clean, well-targeted repair executed by a single mechanical substitution - 'candidate' becomes 'row' wherever the composite draft could otherwise be bundled. That substitution is right for four of the five candidates and for all three rows inside the composite. It is wrong for the fifth, because the Windows platform set is the one eligible candidate that carries owner roles without carrying a file-08 row, and D-096 said so expressly. The fix is not to undo the ADV-D100-01 landing but to make row-keying the composite candidate's special case rather than the base rule, restoring candidate-keying underneath it. That is a two-clause edit that leaves every anti-bundling sentence intact.
